new_with_area.brief: Creates a new `GtkTreeViewColumn` using `area` to render its cells.
new_with_area.md: Creates a new `GtkTreeViewColumn` using `area` to render its cells.

new_with_attributes.brief: Creates a new `GtkTreeViewColumn` with a number of default values.

doc.brief: A visible column in a [`TreeView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TreeView) widget
doc.deprecated_md:
Use [`ColumnView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColumnView) and [`ColumnViewColumn`](xref:gtk:Gtk.ColumnViewColumn)
  instead of [`TreeView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TreeView) to show a tabular list
doc.md:
A visible column in a [`TreeView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TreeView) widget

The `GtkTreeViewColumn` object represents a visible column in a `GtkTreeView` widget.
It allows to set properties of the column header, and functions as a holding pen
for the cell renderers which determine how the data in the column is displayed.

Please refer to the [tree widget conceptual overview](section-tree-widget.html)
for an overview of all the objects and data types related to the tree widget and
how they work together, and to the [`TreeView`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TreeView) documentation for specifics
about the CSS node structure for treeviews and their headers.

add_attribute.brief: Adds an attribute mapping to the list in `tree_column`.
add_attribute.md:
Adds an attribute mapping to the list in `tree_column`.

The `column` is the
column of the model to get a value from, and the `attribute` is the
parameter on `cell_renderer` to be set from the value. So for example
if column 2 of the model contains strings, you could have the
“text” attribute of a `GtkCellRendererText` get its values from
column 2.

cell_get_position.brief: Obtains the horizontal position and size of a cell in a column.
cell_get_position.md:
Obtains the horizontal position and size of a cell in a column.

If the  cell is not found in the column, `start_pos` and `width`
are not changed and `FALSE` is returned.

cell_get_size.brief: Obtains the width and height needed to render the column.
cell_get_size.md:
Obtains the width and height needed to render the column.  This is used
primarily by the `GtkTreeView`.

cell_is_visible.brief: Returns `TRUE` if any of the cells packed into the `tree_column` are visible.
cell_is_visible.md:
Returns `TRUE` if any of the cells packed into the `tree_column` are visible.
For this to be meaningful, you must first initialize the cells with
gtk_tree_view_column_cell_set_cell_data()

cell_set_cell_data.brief: Sets the cell renderer based on the `tree_model` and `iter`.
cell_set_cell_data.md:
Sets the cell renderer based on the `tree_model` and `iter`.  That is, for
every attribute mapping in `tree_column`, it will get a value from the set
column on the `iter`, and use that value to set the attribute on the cell
renderer.  This is used primarily by the `GtkTreeView`.

clear.brief: Unsets all the mappings on all renderers on the `tree_column`.
clear.md: Unsets all the mappings on all renderers on the `tree_column`.

clear_attributes.brief: Clears all existing attributes previously set with gtk_tree_view_column_set_attributes().
clear_attributes.md:
Clears all existing attributes previously set with
gtk_tree_view_column_set_attributes().

clicked.brief: Emits the “clicked” signal on the column.
clicked.md:
Emits the “clicked” signal on the column.  This function will only work if
`tree_column` is clickable.

focus_cell.brief: Sets the current keyboard focus to be at `cell`, if the column contains 2 or more editable and activatable cells.
focus_cell.md:
Sets the current keyboard focus to be at `cell`, if the column contains
2 or more editable and activatable cells.

get_alignment.brief: Returns the current x alignment of `tree_column`.
get_alignment.md:
Returns the current x alignment of `tree_column`.  This value can range
between 0.0 and 1.0.

get_button.brief: Returns the button used in the treeview column header
get_button.md: Returns the button used in the treeview column header

get_clickable.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the user can click on the header for the column.
get_clickable.md: Returns `TRUE` if the user can click on the header for the column.

get_expand.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the column expands to fill available space.
get_expand.md: Returns `TRUE` if the column expands to fill available space.

get_fixed_width.brief: Gets the fixed width of the column.
get_fixed_width.md:
Gets the fixed width of the column.  This may not be the actual displayed
width of the column; for that, use gtk_tree_view_column_get_width().

get_max_width.brief: Returns the maximum width in pixels of the `tree_column`, or -1 if no maximum width is set.
get_max_width.md:
Returns the maximum width in pixels of the `tree_column`, or -1 if no maximum
width is set.

get_min_width.brief: Returns the minimum width in pixels of the `tree_column`, or -1 if no minimum width is set.
get_min_width.md:
Returns the minimum width in pixels of the `tree_column`, or -1 if no minimum
width is set.

get_reorderable.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the `tree_column` can be reordered by the user.
get_reorderable.md: Returns `TRUE` if the `tree_column` can be reordered by the user.

get_resizable.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the `tree_column` can be resized by the end user.
get_resizable.md: Returns `TRUE` if the `tree_column` can be resized by the end user.

get_sort_column_id.brief: Gets the logical `sort_column_id` that the model sorts on when this column is selected for sorting.
get_sort_column_id.md:
Gets the logical `sort_column_id` that the model sorts on
when this column is selected for sorting.

See [`TreeViewColumn.set_sort_column_id()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TreeViewColumn#method:set_sort_column_id).

get_sort_order.brief: Gets the value set by gtk_tree_view_column_set_sort_order().
get_sort_order.md: Gets the value set by gtk_tree_view_column_set_sort_order().

get_title.brief: Returns the title of the widget.
get_title.md: Returns the title of the widget.

get_tree_view.brief: Returns the `GtkTreeView` wherein `tree_column` has been inserted.
get_tree_view.md:
Returns the `GtkTreeView` wherein `tree_column` has been inserted.
If `column` is currently not inserted in any tree view, `NULL` is
returned.

get_widget.brief: Returns the `GtkWidget` in the button on the column header.
get_widget.md:
Returns the `GtkWidget` in the button on the column header.

If a custom widget has not been set then `NULL` is returned.

get_width.brief: Returns the current size of `tree_column` in pixels.
get_width.md: Returns the current size of `tree_column` in pixels.

get_x_offset.brief: Returns the current X offset of `tree_column` in pixels.
get_x_offset.md: Returns the current X offset of `tree_column` in pixels.

pack_end.brief: Adds the `cell` to end of the column.
pack_end.md:
Adds the `cell` to end of the column. If `expand` is `FALSE`, then the `cell`
is allocated no more space than it needs. Any unused space is divided
evenly between cells for which `expand` is `TRUE`.

pack_start.brief: Packs the `cell` into the beginning of the column.
pack_start.md:
Packs the `cell` into the beginning of the column. If `expand` is `FALSE`, then
the `cell` is allocated no more space than it needs. Any unused space is divided
evenly between cells for which `expand` is `TRUE`.

queue_resize.brief: Flags the column, and the cell renderers added to this column, to have their sizes renegotiated.
queue_resize.md:
Flags the column, and the cell renderers added to this column, to have
their sizes renegotiated.

set_alignment.brief: Sets the alignment of the title or custom widget inside the column header.
set_alignment.md:
Sets the alignment of the title or custom widget inside the column header.
The alignment determines its location inside the button -- 0.0 for left, 0.5
for center, 1.0 for right.

set_attributes.brief: Sets the attributes in the list as the attributes of `tree_column`.
set_attributes.md:
Sets the attributes in the list as the attributes of `tree_column`.

The attributes should be in attribute/column order, as in
gtk_tree_view_column_add_attribute(). All existing attributes
are removed, and replaced with the new attributes.

set_cell_data_func.brief: Sets the `GtkTreeCellDataFunc` to use for the column.
set_cell_data_func.md:
Sets the `GtkTreeCellDataFunc` to use for the column.

This
function is used instead of the standard attributes mapping for
setting the column value, and should set the value of `tree_column`'s
cell renderer as appropriate.  `func` may be `NULL` to remove an
older one.

set_clickable.brief: Sets the header to be active if `clickable` is `TRUE`.
set_clickable.md:
Sets the header to be active if `clickable` is `TRUE`.  When the header is
active, then it can take keyboard focus, and can be clicked.

set_expand.brief: Sets the column to take available extra space.
set_expand.md:
Sets the column to take available extra space.  This space is shared equally
amongst all columns that have the expand set to `TRUE`.  If no column has this
option set, then the last column gets all extra space.  By default, every
column is created with this `FALSE`.

Along with “fixed-width”, the “expand” property changes when the column is
resized by the user.

set_fixed_width.brief: If `fixed_width` is not -1, sets the fixed width of `tree_column`; otherwise unsets it.
set_fixed_width.md:
If `fixed_width` is not -1, sets the fixed width of `tree_column`; otherwise
unsets it.  The effective value of `fixed_width` is clamped between the
minimum and maximum width of the column; however, the value stored in the
“fixed-width” property is not clamped.  If the column sizing is
%GTK_TREE_VIEW_COLUMN_GROW_ONLY or %GTK_TREE_VIEW_COLUMN_AUTOSIZE, setting
a fixed width overrides the automatically calculated width.  Note that
`fixed_width` is only a hint to GTK; the width actually allocated to the
column may be greater or less than requested.

Along with “expand”, the “fixed-width” property changes when the column is
resized by the user.

set_max_width.brief: Sets the maximum width of the `tree_column`.
set_max_width.md:
Sets the maximum width of the `tree_column`.  If `max_width` is -1, then the
maximum width is unset.  Note, the column can actually be wider than max
width if it’s the last column in a view.  In this case, the column expands to
fill any extra space.

set_min_width.brief: Sets the minimum width of the `tree_column`.
set_min_width.md:
Sets the minimum width of the `tree_column`.  If `min_width` is -1, then the
minimum width is unset.

set_reorderable.brief: If `reorderable` is `TRUE`, then the column can be reordered by the end user dragging the header.
set_reorderable.md:
If `reorderable` is `TRUE`, then the column can be reordered by the end user
dragging the header.

set_resizable.brief: If `resizable` is `TRUE`, then the user can explicitly resize the column by grabbing the outer edge of the column button.
set_resizable.md:
If `resizable` is `TRUE`, then the user can explicitly resize the column by
grabbing the outer edge of the column button.

If resizable is `TRUE` and
sizing mode of the column is %GTK_TREE_VIEW_COLUMN_AUTOSIZE, then the sizing
mode is changed to %GTK_TREE_VIEW_COLUMN_GROW_ONLY.

set_sizing.brief: Sets the growth behavior of `tree_column` to `type`.
set_sizing.md: Sets the growth behavior of `tree_column` to `type`.

set_sort_column_id.brief: Sets the logical `sort_column_id` that this column sorts on when this column is selected for sorting.
set_sort_column_id.md:
Sets the logical `sort_column_id` that this column sorts on when this column
is selected for sorting.  Doing so makes the column header clickable.

set_sort_indicator.brief: Call this function with a `setting` of `TRUE` to display an arrow in the header button indicating the column is sorted.
set_sort_indicator.md:
Call this function with a `setting` of `TRUE` to display an arrow in
the header button indicating the column is sorted. Call
gtk_tree_view_column_set_sort_order() to change the direction of
the arrow.

set_sort_order.brief: Changes the appearance of the sort indicator.
set_sort_order.md:
Changes the appearance of the sort indicator.

This does not actually sort the model.  Use
gtk_tree_view_column_set_sort_column_id() if you want automatic sorting
support.  This function is primarily for custom sorting behavior, and should
be used in conjunction with gtk_tree_sortable_set_sort_column_id() to do
that. For custom models, the mechanism will vary.

The sort indicator changes direction to indicate normal sort or reverse sort.
Note that you must have the sort indicator enabled to see anything when
calling this function; see gtk_tree_view_column_set_sort_indicator().

set_spacing.brief: Sets the spacing field of `tree_column`, which is the number of pixels to place between cell renderers packed into it.
set_spacing.md:
Sets the spacing field of `tree_column`, which is the number of pixels to
place between cell renderers packed into it.

set_title.md:
Sets the title of the `tree_column`.  If a custom widget has been set, then
this value is ignored.

set_widget.brief: Sets the widget in the header to be `widget`.
set_widget.md:
Sets the widget in the header to be `widget`.  If widget is `NULL`, then the
header button is set with a `GtkLabel` set to the title of `tree_column`.

cell-area.brief: The `GtkCellArea` used to layout cell renderers for this column.
cell-area.md:
The `GtkCellArea` used to layout cell renderers for this column.

If no area is specified when creating the tree view column with gtk_tree_view_column_new_with_area()
a horizontally oriented `GtkCellAreaBox` will be used.

sort-column-id.brief: Logical sort column ID this column sorts on when selected for sorting.
sort-column-id.md:
Logical sort column ID this column sorts on when selected for sorting. Setting the sort column ID makes the column header
clickable. Set to -1 to make the column unsortable.

clicked.brief: Emitted when the column's header has been clicked.
clicked.md: Emitted when the column's header has been clicked.
